title: Saur Revolution
summary: On 27 April 1978 troops allied with the People's Democratic Party of Afghanistan attacked the presidential palace in Kabul. President Daoud and most of his family were shot there the next day. Royal-dynasty rule ended, and a communist-led government took power, which a diplomatic-history source calls a prelude to the Soviet invasion.

uncertainty.note: Sources agree on 27 April; the Library of Congress study places Daoud's death on the following day.

where.modern_name: Kabul, Afghanistan (pin is the city centre, a proxy for the palace and fighting across the city)

importance.justification: Communist-led seizure of power in Afghanistan that preceded the Soviet invasion.

audience_note: Describes a violent coup in which a president and members of his family were killed.
